events.title: UNSUNG: Celebrating the Extraordinary Grandeur of Smallness
events.description:
A photography exhibition curated by Amit Mehra, photographer, curator, and founder of the UNSUNG project, an ongoing initiative that celebrates the lives and contributions of extraordinary yet often overlooked individuals.
The photographs explore the beauty and significance of lives, places, and ideas that often go unnoticed. Through visual narratives by contemporary artists, the exhibition reflects on ordinary people and unseen worlds whose stories reveal resilience, conviction, and human connection.
The exhibition will be inaugurated on Tuesday, 21 July’26 at 18:00 hrs by Amb Shyam Saran, President, IIC
The exhibition will remain open daily from 11:00 to 19:00 hrs
(Collaboration: Srishti Manipal Institute of Art, Design and Technology (a constituent of MAHE, Manipal) and Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE), Manipal (Institution of Eminence Deemed to be University)

events.title: Flux of Being
events.description:
A Solo Exhibition by Ravi Kant Jha, National award-winning artist, his practice investigates themes of consciousness, memory, and transformation.
The exhibition presents a series of paintings that explore consciousness as a state of constant transformation. Through fluid forms, layered compositions, and evocative color fields, the works blur the boundaries between memory, imagination, and reality.
The exhibition will be inaugurated on Saturday, 25 July’26 at 17:00 hrs
The exhibition will remain open daily from 11:00 to 19:00 hrs

events.title: Twamaham Vande
events.description:
A journey for the search of One through the vision of two
Concept, direction and performance by Jalsa Chandra, renowned Bharatanatyam and Kathak dancer, choreographer, fellow of Ministry of Culture and empanelled artiste of ICCR and Doordarshan. Trained under eminent gurus including Smt. Thankamani Kutty, Pt. Rajendra Kumar Gangani, Smt. Nandini Ramani, Padma Shri Chitra Visweswaran, Smt. Rama Vaidyanathan, and Padma Bhushan Saroja Vaidyanathan.
Accompanying artistes: Pallabi Chatterjee, Adrija Mondal and Agnimita Das
The performance presents a soulful journey of the maturing spirit, exploring the "one-to-one realization of God" through the timeless wisdom of Bhakti saints. This production weaves together the cosmic rhythms of the Nasadiya Sukta with the intricate "Deha Tatwa" of Lalon Fakir to depict the cyclical nature of creation. From the unwavering faith of Sita to the Thevaram in celebration of the liberation to find and love the Divine in one's own light. The journey culminates in the oneness of the Parabrahman, where individual identities dissolve like rivers into the vast ocean.

events.title: Bhupen Da Uncut
events.description: Birth Centenary of Dr. Bhupen Hazarika . Bhupen Da Uncut (Docu/2025/Assamese with English subtitles/65 mins) Dir. Bobbeeta Sharma . A rare, vintage first-person account filmed 25 years ago in London, where the legendary maestro reflects on his extraordinary journey. The documentary follows Dr. Hazarika as he speaks intimately about his childhood, the profound influence of Assamese cinema pioneer Jyoti Prasad Agarwala, his higher studies in New York, and the dynamics of his relationship with his wife, Priyamvada Patel. Offering a window into his mind and philosophy, Bhupen Da Uncut features the legend reciting several of his unpublished poems, capturing the essence of the man and his masterpieces. Screening followed by a discussion with Bobbeeta Sharma , director; Chinmoy Sharma , executive producer; Ravindra Badgaiyan , editor .

events.title: The Big Fat City
events.description: The Big Fat City (Hindi/90 mins) Wri. Mahesh Dattani . Dir. Shilpi Marwaha . A thought-provoking drama that explores the complexities of urban life in Mumbai. The story revolves around Murli and his wife, who are struggling to pay off their loan after Murli loses his job. Desperate for financial help, they host a dinner for Murli’s former collegemate, hoping he can secure them another loan. The arrival of their neighbour, a TV actress with her own financial troubles and a drunken husband, complicates the situation. The play explores how financial stress strains relationships while revealing the harsh realities behind the glamourized version of city life. Prod. Sukhmanch Theatre . Tickets at Rs.500, Rs.350 & Rs.200 are available online on bookmyshow.com and at the Habitat Programmes desk .

events.title: She Walked Anyway
events.description: Book Launch & Discussion . She Walked Anyway by Dr. Sazina Khan . A collection of poems and a lyrical meditation on quiet courage, inner reclamation, and the profound strength of moving forward without permission or validation. Through evocative poems such as Unannounced Becoming, Permissionless, Grace, Unrequested, The Yes I Gave Myself, and Becoming Without Allowance , this collection traces the inner evolution of a woman who chooses motion over hesitation and self-trust over approval. Publisher: White Falcon . The author will be in conversation on Walking Through Storms: Women, Memory and the Making of the Inner Self with Oroon Das , actor, theatre artist and Dr. Gilles Chuyen , director, choreographer, actor. Moderator: Meera Khanna , writer, poet, Trustee & President, The Guild for Service. Chief Guest: Prof. (Dr.) K. G. Suresh , Director, India Habitat Centre.

events.title: The House of Bernarda Alba
events.description: The House of Bernarda Alba (English/130 mins with interval) Design & Direction by Shomik Ray . Written by Spanish playwright, Federico García Lorca in June 1936, during the turbulent period of the Spanish Revolution. The play explores domestic oppression, love, desire, and betrayal while serving as a powerful reflection on authoritarian systems that suppress individual voices in the name of society. Through Bernarda Alba’s household, Lorca examines themes of power, control, repression, and the human longing for freedom, combining emotional conflict, dark humour, and violence into a timeless theatrical experience. Prod. Shapno Ekhon . Tickets at Rs.500, Rs.350 & Rs.200 are available online on bookmyshow.com and at the Habitat Programmes desk .

Moderator: Shubha Chaudhuri, Associate Director General (Academic), Archives and Research Centre for Ethnomusicology, American Institute of Indian Studies
The speaker will share their experience studying the Western Tibetan folk lute gowo (called ko-phongs in Ladakhi) in Ladakh, and the repatriation of musical recordings made between the 1930s and 1970s. The talk will explore the significance of these recordings in understanding the instrument's diverse performance styles, song ecologies and heritage narratives.

Uniting Science, Health, Policy & People

Ganesan, Chairman, Haryana State Pollution Control Board; Amit Bhatt, India Managing Director, International Council on Clean Transportation; Trupti Deshpande, Energiva Ventures
Transitioning to clean urban mobility yields profound benefits—ranging from improved air quality and reduced greenhouse gas emissions to quieter and more livable cities. This session will explore how to accelerate the shift toward zero-emission transport by scaling up electric vehicle ecosystems, modernizing public transit networks, and enforcing stringent emission regulations.
This is the fourth discussion in the series of dialogues under the umbrella of ‘Uniting Science, Health, Policy & People’

events.title: Sargun se Nirgun: Kabir in Motion
events.description: Sargun se Nirgun: Kabir in Motion. A Bharatanatyam performance by Bhadra Sinha and Gayathri Sharma , exploring the philosophy of Sant Kabir as a journey from ignorance to awareness, and from ritual to realization. Rooted in Bhakti, Kabir's verses transcend religion, and through expressive abhinaya, rhythmic footwork, and symbolic choreography, the performance highlights the enduring relevance of his teachings in modern life. Collab. Kalakriti Arts and Satyanjali Trust .

events.title: Rashtra Yajna: Every Step in Service, Every Beat for the Nation
events.description: Rashtra Yajna: Every Step in Service, Every Beat for the Nation . To Commemorate the 150th Anniversary of Vande Mataram . Woven with the grace, discipline and expressive power of Bharatanatyam, the performance transforms every movement into an offering of devotion and every rhythmic beat into a tribute to the spirit of the Nation. Enriched by the immediacy and emotional depth of live musicians, the production celebrates India's invaluable cultural heritage, orally transmitted for thousands of years, now inscribed in the Memory of the World (MOW) by UNESCO, the sacrifices of its freedom fighters, and the enduring ideals of beauty, nature's bounty, unity and nationalism. Presented by IHC in collaboration with Prathibha Prahlad & Prasiddha Repertory .

events.title: Dalla Ayaara
events.description: Dalla Ayaara (Hindustani, Urdu/40 mins) Performed by Meera Rizvi & Usman Siddiqui . Followed by Dastan - e - Chhabeeli Bhatiyarin (Hindustani, Urdu/50 mins) Performed by Meera Rizvi & Rana Pratap Sengar . Adapted by Meera Rizvi . Dir. Mahmood Farooqui . Produced by Anusha Rizvi . Two hilarious qissas from the 19th century about wily women and their stratagems. Dalla Ayaara is witty, quick-thinking, and charming, and manages to con anyone and everyone who crosses her path, often with hilarious results. Chhabeeli is a qissa where the story pits the other woman (Chhabeeli) and the Prince’s wife (Nachhattar) against each other in a contest of wits as they compete to win the affections of a rather entitled and silly Prince. Prod. Dastangoi Collective . Tickets at Rs.500, Rs.350 & Rs.200 are available online on bookmyshow.com and at the Habitat Programmes desk .

events.title: Dastan - e - Raahi
events.description: Dastan - e - Raahi (Hindustani, Urdu, Bhojpuri/90 mins with interval) Adapted by Darain Shahidi . Performed by Darain Shahidi & Rajesh Kumar . Dir. Mahmood Farooqui . Produced by Anusha Rizvi . Celebrating the centenary of the great Hindi writer Dr. Rahi Masoom Raza, this Dastangoi performance traces his extraordinary journey from his childhood in Gangauli to his years as an uncompromising academic and the legendary writer who gave us the rustic soul of Aadha Gaon , a landmark of Hindi literature. It narrates his remarkable career as a writer and lyricist in the Bombay film industry, culminating in his screenplay and dialogues for B. R. Chopra's epoch-defining television serial Mahabharata . Prod. Dastangoi Collective . Tickets at Rs.500, Rs.350 & Rs.200 are available online on bookmyshow.com and at the Habitat Programmes desk .

events.title: Hansika: An Adaptation of Swan Lake
events.description: Hansika: An Adaptation of Swan Lake (English/75 mins) Choreographed by Sharmila Mukerjee , performed by her with the Sanjali Ensemble. Original Music Score & Direction by Praveen D Rao . Hansika is an adaptation of Swan Lake, the ballet composed by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, in the context of Indian classical dance–Odissi. Inspired by the story of Odette, a princess turned into a swan by an evil sorcerer's curse, the production explores the humane aspect of the plot through the Indian world of raga, taal, laya and rasa. Prod. Sanjali Centre for Odissi Dance . Tickets at Rs.500, Rs.400 & Rs.250 are available online on bookmyshow.com and at the Habitat Programmes desk.
